title: Tartiroi of Mahalul
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Mentioned in Maaser Sheni, chapter 5, at the beginning of halakhah 2: he would go up to spend the Sabbath in the Temple, yet nobody would get up for the figs before him. Hyman says Mahalul is a place near Jerusalem, as explained there.

notes.text: The Hebrew and the consulted Guggenheimer translation describe spending the Sabbath in the Temple and returning early for figs. Hyman places Mahalul near Jerusalem, while that edition’s note places Malul in lower Galilee. The conflicting geography is not resolved or adopted canonically. The translated edition calls Tartiroi “the cap maker”; the supplied heading remains transliterated.

The earlier named Guggenheimer comparison describes Sabbath in the Temple and early return for figs; its note places Malul in Lower Galilee, whereas Hyman says near Jerusalem. These remain attributed conflicting geographic claims, not a canonical location. That edition’s cap-maker interpretation is not inserted into the supplied Tartiroi heading. רה״ב is beginning of halakhah2 and בי״מהק is contextually the Temple; no new whole primary witness or historical-geographic adjudication is claimed.

The Hebrew of Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 5:2 and Guggenheimer’s translation both connect the Sabbath in the Temple with getting up early for the figs. Guggenheimer’s notes interpret Tartiroi as “cap maker” and place Malul in Lower Galilee. Hyman’s printed notice places Mahalul near Jerusalem. The two geographic claims remain open.
